Notes: c. 1st c. CE (midpoint 50 CE; palaeographic date). P.Oxy. L 3522 (Rahlfs 857), a fragment of Greek Job 42:11-12 with two occurrences of the Tetragrammaton written in paleo-Hebrew script; Meyer (McMaster PhD thesis 2017) dates it to the first century CE, says it is 'likely from Oxyrhynchus' and counts it among the c. fifteen Jewish-Greek literary manuscripts of the 2nd c. BCE - end of 1st c. CE, which come mainly from the Fayyum and Oxyrhynchus (ed. Parsons, P.Oxy. L, 1983, pp. 1-3). Evidence of Jewish readers/scribes of Scripture in the city; suggests a literate Jewish community but gives no size. Year Established = 50 CE: this is the earliest datable evidence for Jews in the city itself found in accessible sources. Not used for Year Established: P.Oxy. X 1281 (CPJ no. 414), a loan of 300 dr. by 'Joseph' (probably a Jew) to a linen-weaver, dated 21 CE (8th year of Tiberius) but drawn up at the village of Sinaru in the Oxyrhynchite nome, so Joseph's residence in the city is not documented; and a Ptolemaic Aramaic ostracon from Oxyrhynchus listed in Porten-Yardeni TAD vol. 4, which Meyer mentions but does not identify as Jewish. Outside the period: Diaspora revolt reaching the Oxyrhynchite nome 115-117 CE and a synagogue at Oxyrhynchus attested by papyrus in 291 CE. No population figure for the Jews of Oxyrhynchus in the Second Temple period was found.

c. 1st c. CE (midpoint 50 CE). P.Oxy. LXXVII 5101 (Rahlfs 2227), Greek Psalter (portions of 56 verses) with at least three occurrences of the Tetragrammaton in paleo-Hebrew script; Meyer dates it palaeographically to the first century CE ('the earliest extant witness to the Greek Psalter'), 'likely' from Oxyrhynchus, and treats it as a Jewish-Greek manuscript (ed. Colomo and Henry, P.Oxy. LXXVII, 2011). Note: other descriptions date it more broadly to mid-1st - mid-2nd c. CE, so it may postdate 70 CE. A second Jewish scriptural manuscript from the city; no community size implied.
